$comment: Organisations that have asked NOT to be listed, or not to be contacted, or both.
THIS FILE IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NEVER BE 'CLEANED UP'.
It is the reason a removal request actually sticks. Without it the failure mode is obvious and
inevitable: someone asks to be removed, the entry is deleted from the prose, and three months
later a refresh re-scrapes the same public web page and puts them straight back. That would be
worse than never offering removal at all, because it converts a promise into a broken one.
So it is enforced in TWO places, both of which fail closed:
1. build.js REFUSES TO BUILD if a suppressed address or organisation name appears in the
rendered page. Not a warning - the page does not get built. The guard sits at the point
where the harm would occur, which is publication.
2. notify-listed.js never writes to anyone listed here, whatever the ledger says.
ENTRIES ARE NEVER DELETED. An organisation that asks to come back gets scope changed to
'none' with a dated note - the record of the original request stays, because it is the evidence
that the request was honoured.
FIELDS
id        matches data/actors.json where one existed; a free slug otherwise
name      organisation name, matched case-insensitively against rendered output
emails    addresses that must never be published or written to
scope     'listing-and-contact' - remove entirely, never contact
'contact-only'        - may stay listed, but never email them
'contact-details'     - may stay listed by name, but publish no contact details
'none'                - previously suppressed, since withdrawn (keep the history)
requestedOn   when they asked
requestedVia  'email-reply' | 'form' | 'direct' - how the request arrived
note          anything the next maintainer needs to know
